title: Indonesia’s top graft prosecutor resigns as police probe widens
article:
(July 11): Indonesia’s top corruption prosecutor has resigned, days after a police raid of his house uncovered gold bars and millions of dollars in cash.

Febrie Adriansyah stepped down as junior attorney general for the Special Crimes division, the Attorney General’s Office said Saturday. His departure is intended to safeguard the integrity, objectivity and neutrality of law enforcement while police investigations continue, it said. The statement didn’t mention a successor.

Adriansyah’s departure is the biggest fallout yet from a widening investigation that has drawn the country’s police, prosecutors and military into a rare public controversy. Police have searched more than a dozen locations and seized gold, cash, and foreign currencies while investigating alleged corruption and money laundering involving several state-linked companies.

Febrie was one of Indonesia’s highest-profile corruption prosecutors, overseeing the Attorney General’s Office unit that handles major graft cases, including probes involving state miner Timah, oil company Pertamina and airline Garuda Indonesia. He had also led the charge in cases involving former Education Minister Nadiem Makarim and President Prabowo Subianto’s free-meals programme.

At a house south of Jakarta that Adriansyah acknowledged belonged to him, investigators found 74 kilogrammes of gold bars along with cash and foreign currencies in seven suitcases locked in a safe, with the total haul valued at about US$26.3 million. Adriansyah denied owning the seized assets.

Police have said the raids were linked to at least three corruption and money-laundering investigations, including alleged coal-supply graft tied to recent power blackouts. They haven’t publicly said which investigation is directly linked to Adriansyah, nor have they announced any suspects.

The controversy intensified after armed military personnel were deployed outside another residence linked to Febrie in Jakarta. The military said the deployment was requested by the Attorney General’s Office under regulations governing protection for prosecutors and denied interfering with the police investigation.

Adriansyah had led the Attorney General’s Office’s Special Crimes division since 2022 and his resignation raises questions over who will take charge of those cases. The Attorney General’s Office said the unit would continue operating normally, according to the statement on Saturday.
